items.rationale: The watch was taken by threat of force away from home (2.3.1–2.3.2). Its like-for-like value exceeds the €2,500 unscheduled valuables limit in 4.2.2; the watch and ring together reach, but do not exceed, the €5,000 event limit.

The €3,850 receipt supports a like-for-like value above the €2,500 per-item limit under 4.2.2 and 6.2.3. The two covered valuables total €5,000 after the per-item limits, so no further reduction applies.
The necklace was found missing separately and was not taken in the robbery. Clauses 2.3.4(a) and 7.1.10 exclude the loss, so it does not share the valuables limit.
Under 4.2.3 and 6.2.4, the approximately €1,200 nominal cash loss is capped at €500 per event. No deductible applies.

The phone is covered as a general household effect under 4.2.1, and the €10,000 away-from-home limit does not bind. For a two-year-old phone bought for about €700, I estimate €475 at current value under 6.2.2, with any replacement-value uplift subject to proof under 7.6.

items.description: Replacement travel and extra hotel nights
items.rationale: Clause 3.1.7 excludes both rearranged travel and additional accommodation. The hotel benefit in 5.2.5 applies only when insured physical damage makes the insured home uninhabitable.
Clause 7.1.8(b) excludes separately billed shipping, whether for replacement property or for documents.
The police report is required under 2.3.3, but 3.1.6 and 7.1.8(f) expressly exclude the cost of translating it for the claim.
Clauses 3.1.6 and 7.1.8(f) expressly exclude notarising or certifying supporting documents for the claim.
The translation provider's working materials are excluded under 7.1.8(e)–(f); they are not materials used to repair insured property.
Clauses 3.1.5–3.1.6 and 7.1.8(e) exclude separately billed administration and claim processing.
